```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

# The walkthrough runs the CTAS engine, so it needs the gsm framework and the
# SDTM test data. Chunks are skipped rather than failed when they are missing,
# so the vignette still builds on a minimal machine.
bRun <- all(vapply(
  c("gsm.core", "gsm.mapping", "pharmaversesdtm", "workr", "arrow"),
  requireNamespace,
  logical(1),
  quietly = TRUE
))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = bRun)
```

`gsm.ctas` runs the [ctas](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctas) anomaly
detection engine inside the [gsm](https://github.com/Gilead-BioStats/gsm.core)
workflow framework and writes the three files
[ctasapp](https://github.com/IMPALA-Consortium/ctasapp) reads.

This vignette walks the whole path -- SDTM domains in, ctasapp shards out --
and covers the two things most users will want to change: the CTAS features
each metric scores, and the set of metrics.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("IMPALA-Consortium/gsm.ctas")
```

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(gsm.ctas)
```

## The shape of the pipeline

gsm is a YAML-driven engine: each layer is a directory of workflow files, and
`RunWorkflows()` executes them in order.

```
lRaw --Ingest--> lIngest --1_mappings--> lMapped --2_metrics--> lAnalysis
     --3_reporting--> ctasapp shards on disk
```

`gsm.ctas` ships three layers in `inst/workflow/`:

| Layer | Contents |
|---|---|
| `1_mappings` | SDTM readers (`DM`, `VS`, `LB`), site/study group tables, plus the transformation-typed frames `Subjects`, `Numeric`, `Range` |
| `2_metrics` | One YAML per data-type transformation (`numeric`, `range_normalized`, `ratio_missing`), each running CTAS once |
| `3_reporting` | `Write_Results`: bind ctasapp shards across metrics and write to disk |

Each metric emits three flat frames in the shape ctasapp reads:
`results`, `input` and `untransformed`. The reporting layer binds them across
metrics and writes them as parquet.

## Input data

`pharmaversesdtm` provides the SDTM domains. The example is cut down to six
sites and a handful of tests to keep the engine fast.

```{r data}
vSites <- sort(unique(pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID))[1:6]

dfDM <- pharmaversesdtm::dm[pharmaversesdtm::dm$SITEID %in% vSites, ]
dfVS <- pharmaversesdtm::vs[
  pharmaversesdtm::vs$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::vs$VSTESTCD %in% c("SYSBP", "DIABP", "PULSE"),
]
dfLB <- pharmaversesdtm::lb[
  pharmaversesdtm::lb$USUBJID %in% dfDM$USUBJID &
    pharmaversesdtm::lb$LBTESTCD %in% c("ALB", "BILI", "CREAT"),
]

lRaw <- list(
  Raw_DM = as.data.frame(dfDM),
  Raw_VS = as.data.frame(dfVS),
  Raw_LB = as.data.frame(dfLB)
)
```

## 1. Mapping

```{r mappings}
lMappingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/1_mappings", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lIngest <- gsm.mapping::Ingest(
  lRaw, gsm.mapping::CombineSpecs(lMappingWorkflows)
)

# CTAS emits `cor()` "standard deviation is zero" warnings for flat series.
lMapped <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMappingWorkflows, lData = lIngest)
)

names(lMapped)
```

`Mapped_Subjects` is the shared subject/site frame; `Mapped_VS` and `Mapped_LB`
are the SDTM domain frames (with unscheduled visits filtered) that each metric
YAML pulls from directly via column overrides.

## 2. Metrics

Each metric YAML runs CTAS once for its data type and emits the ctasapp shards.
The data-type transform is a three-step chain: `Standardize_Domain()` renames
the SDTM columns to the CTAS long-format vocabulary and joins subject
metadata, `Input_Numeric()` / `Input_Range()` / `Input_Missing()` adds the
`result` and category columns, and `Analyze_CTAS()` scores the sites. Adding
another numeric source (e.g. EG) is a metric-YAML edit, not a mapping-YAML
one.

```{r metrics}
lMetricWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/2_metrics", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

lAnalysis <- suppressWarnings(
  gsm.core::RunWorkflows(lWorkflows = lMetricWorkflows, lData = lMapped)
)

names(lAnalysis)
names(lAnalysis$Analysis_numeric)
```

Feature selection is one boolean per CTAS feature in `meta:`, so any metric
can toggle features individually:

```yaml
meta:
  ID: numeric
  FeatureAutocorr: true
  FeatureAverage: true
  FeatureSD: true
  FeatureRange: false
  FeatureUniqueValueCountRelative: true
  FeatureOwnSiteSimilScore: false
  FeatureLOF: false
```

Multi-study is honoured automatically: when `Mapped_Subjects` contains several
values in `studyid`, `Analyze_CTAS()` splits the input by study, runs CTAS on
each, and stacks the results with a `study` column tagged onto every row.

## 3. Reporting: writing ctasapp shards

`Write_Results()` binds the three shards across every metric and writes them
to disk. Parquet is the default because `input` grows quickly.

```{r reporting, eval = FALSE}
Write_Results(lAnalysis, strDir = "ctas_shards", strFormat = "parquet")
```

The equivalent workflow, driven from YAML:

```{r reporting_yaml, eval = FALSE}
lReportingWorkflows <- workr::MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = NULL,
  strPath = system.file("workflow/3_reporting", package = "gsm.ctas"),
  strPackage = NULL
)

gsm.core::RunWorkflows(
  lWorkflows = lReportingWorkflows,
  lData = list(
    lAnalyzed = lAnalysis, strDir = "ctas_shards", strFormat = "parquet"
  )
)
```

The three files map straight onto the ctasapp upload contract:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `results.parquet` | One row per (site x timeseries x feature); site scores joined to `parameter_id` and category labels. |
| `input.parquet` | The CTAS run's `data`, joined to `subjects` and `parameters`, so ctasapp can plot the underlying series. |
| `untransformed.parquet` | Original values recorded by `Input_Range()`, for showing lab results in their own units next to the normalised value. Omitted when no metric produced any. |

`queries` is optional and external -- typically an EDC export -- and can be
handed to `Write_Results()` via `dfQueries` to travel alongside the shards.

## Adding a metric

A new metric is a YAML file, not a function. Copy `numeric.yaml`, change the
`ID`, point it at a mapped frame, and toggle the features it should score:

```yaml
meta:
  ID: my_metric
  FeatureAutocorr: false
  FeatureAverage: true
  FeatureSD: true
  FeatureRange: false
  FeatureUniqueValueCountRelative: true
  FeatureOwnSiteSimilScore: false
  FeatureLOF: false
  MinTimepoints: 3
  MinSubjects: 3
  ...
```

To use your own workflow set, copy `inst/workflow/` and point `workr::MakeWorkflowList()`
at the copy.
